Amir — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short matrix and a staged rollout playbook attached; below is the TL;DR and the things procurement typically asks for.

TL;DR:
- Start: Compact tier + Reranking add-on (no Dedicated). Prefix caching and KV cache (local) preserved across add-on changes.
- Stage 2: Add Dedicated KV cache and increase token throughput (reserved capacity commit). Pricing step = compact base + add-on prorated for current month, then monthly commit starts on the next billing cycle (we can align start to avoid partial-month big uplifts).
- Fallback: Auto-route to Compact variants if Dedicated pool saturated — no integration changes required.

Key asks for procurement/eng:
1) A short SOW for staged rollout (we included a template in the attached PDF).
2) Clear metric gates for each stage (latency P95, error rate, token throughput).
3) A rollback window and a credit schedule if the rollout doesn't meet gates (we usually do a 15% service credit on the initial commit during the pilot-to-dedicated transition if latency SLO is missed).

Attachments: clearline-upgrade-matrix.xlsx (upgrade matrix + cost delta table), staged-rollout-sow-v1.pdf (SOW template with gates).

Ben — see pricing options in sheet tab "staged_pricing"; Priya can coordinate the pilot ops/checkpoints. Kimberly, can you confirm the grace-credit language we can offer for pilot-to-dedicated transitions?

Amir — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the matrix with your procurement team if that helps.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Amir / team — following up with the concrete pricing notes you asked for. Highlights from the "staged_pricing" tab in the matrix:
- Option A (Low friction): Compact + Reranking add-on. Add-on billed monthly at 0.9x list for pilot months; when you convert to Dedicated we credit pilot add-on fees against the first month of the commit (effectively smoothing uplift).
- Option B (Commit-backed): Compact -> Dedicated reserve. We offer a 10% commit discount on the Dedicated baseline if you sign a 6-month commit within the pilot window. That discount is combinable with a 5% pilot-conversion credit.
- Option C (Hybrid ramp): Start metered Compact, nominate a future activation date for Dedicated commit — we cap the maximum effective uplift by pre-agreeing a transition credit schedule.

Grace language (per Logan's ask): we can include a one-time 15% service credit on the first Dedicated month if the rollout fails to meet mutually-agreed gates (applies to Dedicated baseline only, not add-ons).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Amir: pick Option A or B as your preferred path so procurement has a clear ask.
2) I'll generate a short commercial term sheet (1 page) that lists price tables for Option A/B and the credit language.
3) Priya: coordinate a pilot checkpoint at day 14 and day 28 for gate evaluation.

If procurement wants line-item pricing for each add-on and prorate math, I'll attach a plain CSV they can drop into their ERP.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
